title: Affine fibre neighbourhoods detect scheme neighbourhoods under finite locally free covers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:E\to B$ be representable, surjective and finite locally free: for every scheme $T\to B$, the sheaf fibre product $E\times_BT$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is a scheme and its projection to $T$ is surjective and finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Give spaces the atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For each $b\in|B|$, the following are equivalent: (i) there is an open subspace $N\subseteq B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] containing $b$ and represented by a scheme; (ii) there is an open subspace $A\subseteq E$ represented by an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose point set contains the entire inverse image $|p|^{-1}(\{b\})$. No separatedness, Noetherianity, quasi-compactness, or schemeness assumption is imposed on $B$ or $E$.

source.place: Tag 0BA1 (lemma-when-quotient-scheme-at-point), full equivalence; unlike spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 0B87 this needs no group action.

proof.text: Assume (i). Choose an affine open $V$ of the scheme $N$ containing $b$, using the local affine condition in the definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An open subscheme of $N$ is an open subspace of $B$: on each scheme test it is an open subscheme of an open subscheme. By the hypothesis on $p$, $A=E\times_BV$ is a scheme and $A\to V$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], hence finite. A finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and an affine morphism has affine inverse image of an affine open [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; apply this to the whole affine target $V$. Thus $A$ is affine. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], $A$ is open in $E$ with point set $|p|^{-1}(|V|)$, which contains the full fibre over $b$. This proves (ii).

Assume (ii), and set $C=|E|\setminus|A|$. Since $A$ is an open subspace, $|A|$ is an open subset of $|E|$ [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so $C$ is closed. The map $p$ is finite on scheme tests by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Its point map is closed by [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology], so $O=|B|\setminus|p|(C)$ is open. The full-fibre hypothesis gives $b\in O$. Choose a scheme atlas of $B$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Applying [lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient] to this atlas and $O$ produces an open subspace $N\subseteq B$ with $|N|=O$. For any point $e$ of $E$ mapping into $O$, $e\notin C$, since otherwise $p(e)\in|p|(C)$. Hence $|p|^{-1}(|N|)\subseteq|A|$. This complement-image construction directly gives the saturated shrinking in the source.

source.place: Tag 0BA1 (lemma-when-quotient-scheme-at-point), proof, second paragraph: saturated open shrinking

proof.text: Put $W=E\times_BN$. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] it is open in $E$ and has point set $|p|^{-1}(|N|)$. The inclusion of this set in $|A|$ makes $W\to E$ factor through $A$, and the pullback to $A$ is $W$ itself by that same cited statement. Since the inclusion of $W$ is representable by open immersions [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $W$ is therefore a scheme isomorphic to an open subscheme of the affine scheme $A$. For every scheme $T\to N$, the fibre product $W\times_NT$ is canonically $E\times_BT$ by its universal property. Its projection to $T$ is surjective and finite locally free by the original hypothesis on $p$. Surjectivity on every scheme base change is equivalent to surjectivity of $|W|\to|N|$ on point classes [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], which is the form of surjectivity the next citation assumes. Thus $W\to N$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-open-affine-cover], which makes $N$ a scheme. Since $b\in|N|$, (i) follows.

lean.statement: theorem finiteLocallyFree_fibre_scheme_neighbourhood_iff {S : Scheme.{u}} (E B : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : E ⟶ B) (hp : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q ↦ Surjective q.left ∧ q.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree) p.hom.hom) (b : Point B.obj.obj) : (∃ N : OpenSubspace B, b ∈ pointImage N.val.ι ∧ ∃ T : Over S, Nonempty (N.val.toFunctor ≅ yoneda.obj T)) ↔ (∃ A : OpenSubspace E, (∃ T : Over S, IsAffine T.left ∧ Nonempty (A.val.toFunctor ≅ yoneda.obj T)) ∧ ∀ e : PointRepresentative E.obj.obj, Quot.mk _ (e.map p.hom.hom) = b → Quot.mk _ e ∈ pointImage A.val.ι)
lean.note: The scheme-test hypothesis uses IsRepresentableWith with the conjunction of scheme surjectivity and the recorded IsFiniteLocallyFree class. Both open subspaces use the recorded OpenSubspace definition; schemeness is Yoneda representability and affineness is IsAffine on the representing scheme. The full-fibre condition is expressed on all field-valued point representatives, avoiding a second definition of the point map.
